cards.text: Picture it, friend. Tattenai, governor of the region west of the Euphrates, has written to King Darius asking him to check whether King Cyrus ever issued a decree to rebuild the house of God in Jerusalem (Ezra 5:6-17). So Darius orders a search of the archives stored in the treasury of Babylon.

cards.question: Darius has the archives in Babylon searched for Cyrus's decree. Where does the scroll turn up?

cards.text: Ecbatana, in the province of Media. Friend, I lived in a junk drawer, so I've SEEN this: you tear the whole kitchen apart for the scissors, and they're in the OTHER drawer.

cards.question: The scroll is a memo about a decree King Cyrus issued in his first year. Cyrus says to rebuild God's house in Jerusalem as a place for offering ___.
The memo about Cyrus's decree even gives the size of God's house: sixty cubits high and sixty cubits wide. True or false: the Jews have to pay the building costs themselves.

cards.text: There's one more thing in that memo. Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon (Ezra 5:12) had taken things from the temple in Jerusalem and carried them off to Babylon.

cards.question: The memo about Cyrus's decree says the things Nebuchadnezzar carried off to Babylon must go back to the temple in Jerusalem. What are they?

cards.text: So Darius has his answer, and he issues a decree to Tattenai, Shethar-bozenai and their officials. Those are the men who went asking the Jews who authorized all this building (Ezra 5:3-4).

cards.question: King Darius's decree goes to Tattenai, the governor who questioned the Jews about the building. What's the first thing Darius tells him?

answers.text: Stop the work until I come

cards.text: Darius keeps going: "Leave this work on the house of God alone." And the cost gets paid in full from the royal treasury.

cards.question: Darius says the elders building God's house get their costs paid in full, so that the work will not be ___.

cards.text: Here's the part that gets me, friend. That money comes out of the taxes of the provinces west of the Euphrates, and that's Tattenai's own region, so his side is now paying the BILL.

cards.question: Darius also orders young bulls, rams and lambs for burnt offerings, plus wheat, salt, wine and oil. They're given daily, whatever is requested by the ___ in Jerusalem.
True or false: Darius says he's providing these supplies so the priests can also pray for the lives of the king and his sons.

cards.text: So sacrifices of a sweet aroma can go up to the God of heaven. The king is covering the supplies, and he's basically saying, hey, while you're at it, put in a word for me and the boys.
Then Darius adds a warning: if any man interferes with this decree, a beam is to be torn from his house, and he is to be impaled on it.

cards.question: Under Darius's warning, what happens to the house of any man who interferes with the decree?

answers.text: It becomes a pile of rubble

cards.text: Then come Darius's words about God: "May God, who has caused His Name to dwell there…"

cards.question: Darius's words: may God overthrow any king or people who lifts a hand to alter this decree, or to do what?

cards.text: Then he signs off: "Let it be carried out with diligence." That box is SEALED, friend.

King Darius's decree is out, and now the response is up to Tattenai, governor of the region west of the Euphrates, along with Shethar-bozenai and their associates. Friend, the ball is in THEIR court now.

cards.question: True or false: Tattenai and his associates diligently carry out what King Darius decreed.

cards.text: Like the coworker who questioned your whole project suddenly carrying the boxes for you. And with that, the Jewish elders build, and they prosper.

cards.question: The Jewish elders build and prosper through the prophesying of two prophets. Who are they?

With Haggai the prophet and Zechariah son of Iddo prophesying, the elders finish building according to the command of the ___ of Israel and the decrees of Cyrus, Darius and Artaxerxes, kings of Persia.

cards.text: And then, friend, it happens: the house of God is finished. Not almost done, not nearly done, DONE.

cards.question: The temple is completed on the third day of the month of Adar. In which year?

answers.text: The sixth year of King Darius
The first year of King Cyrus

cards.text: The priests, the Levites and the rest of the exiles celebrate the dedication of the house of God with joy. That's me when a whole tray comes out of the oven perfect, except their reason is a WHOLE lot bigger than cookies.

cards.question: For the dedication of the house of God, the people of Israel offer a hundred bulls, two hundred rams and four hundred lambs, plus a sin offering for all Israel of twelve male goats. Why twelve?

answers.text: One for each tribe of Israel
One for each month of the year
One for each gate of Jerusalem

cards.text: With the house dedicated, it's time to get everybody organized. The priests go by their divisions and the Levites by their groups, for the service of God in Jerusalem.

cards.question: True or false: the priests and Levites are organized for the service of God according to King Darius's decree.

cards.text: It's according to what is written in the Book of Moses. Then on the fourteenth day of the first month, the exiles keep the Passover.

cards.question: Before the Passover, what had all the priests and Levites done?
The ___ slaughter the Passover lamb for all the exiles, for their priestly brothers and for themselves.

cards.text: With the lamb slaughtered, friend, now comes the Passover meal itself.

cards.question: True or false: only the Israelites who returned from exile eat the Passover.

cards.text: All who had separated themselves from the uncleanness of the peoples of the land to seek the LORD eat with them. Then for seven days, they keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread with joy.

cards.question: The people keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread with joy. Where does that joy come from?

answers.text: Their neighbors made peace with them

cards.text: The LORD had turned the heart of the king of Assyria toward them, to strengthen their hands in the work on the house of the God of Israel. The house of God is standing again, friend, and no, I'm not crying, I just got flour in my eye.
